### Define sample GET and POST routes

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/guides/testing.md

Defines example GET and POST endpoints on a Hono application to validate in test suites.

```ts
app.get('/posts', (c) => {
  return c.text('Many posts')
})

app.post('/posts', (c) => {
  return c.json(
    {
      message: 'Created',
    },
    201,
    {
      'X-Custom': 'Thank you',
    }
  )
})
```

--------------------------------

### Initialize a Hono app with the CLI

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/agents/cli.md

Use `hono init` to add a Hono app from a create-hono template to an existing project where `npm create hono` cannot be used. The `--template` flag selects the template and `--install` installs dependencies using the package manager from the lockfile or the command that started `hono`. Without `--template`, the template is detected from files in the directory; without a terminal, the error lists the templates.

```sh
npm install -D @hono/cli
npx hono init --template cloudflare-workers --install
npx hono request /
```

### Initialize WebAssembly Hono project and install dependencies

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/getting-started/webassembly-wasi.md

Initializes a new project directory and installs Hono alongside Bytecode Alliance WASI tools and Rolldown. Ensure that `type` is set to `"module"` in `package.json`.

```sh
mkdir my-app
cd my-app
npm init
npm i hono
npm i -D @bytecodealliance/jco @bytecodealliance/componentize-js @bytecodealliance/jco-std
npm i -D rolldown
```

```sh
mkdir my-app
cd my-app
npm init
yarn add hono
yarn add -D @bytecodealliance/jco @bytecodealliance/componentize-js @bytecodealliance/jco-std
yarn add -D rolldown
```

```sh
mkdir my-app
cd my-app
pnpm init --init-type module
pnpm add hono
pnpm add -D @bytecodealliance/jco @bytecodealliance/componentize-js @bytecodealliance/jco-std
pnpm add -D rolldown
```

```sh
mkdir my-app
cd my-app
npm init
bun add hono
bun add -D @bytecodealliance/jco @bytecodealliance/componentize-js @bytecodealliance/jco-std
```

### Create a basic Hono server in main.ts

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/getting-started/deno.md

Define a root route handler returning text and start the HTTP server using Deno.serve with app.fetch.

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'

const app = new Hono()

app.get('/', (c) => c.text('Hello Deno!'))

Deno.serve(app.fetch)
```

### Create a Hello World application in src/index.ts

```ts
import { serve } from '@hono/node-server'
import { Hono } from 'hono'

const app = new Hono()
app.get('/', (c) => c.text('Hello Node.js!'))

serve(app)
```

### Create a Hello World application with fire()

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/getting-started/fastly.md

Defines a basic Fastly Compute entry point in src/index.ts using fire from @fastly/hono-fastly-compute. Use Hono from 'hono' rather than 'hono/quick' because fire builds router data during initialization.

```ts
// src/index.ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'
import { fire } from '@fastly/hono-fastly-compute'

const app = new Hono()

app.get('/', (c) => c.text('Hello Fastly!'))

fire(app)
```

--------------------------------

### Define basic routes and HTTP method handlers

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/api/routing.md

Demonstrates routing by HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, QUERY), wildcard paths, handling all methods with app.all, custom HTTP methods, and handling multiple methods or paths with app.on.

```typescript
import { Hono } from 'hono'
const app = new Hono()
// ---cut---
// HTTP Methods
app.get('/', (c) => c.text('GET /'))
app.post('/', (c) => c.text('POST /'))
app.put('/', (c) => c.text('PUT /'))
app.delete('/', (c) => c.text('DELETE /'))
app.query('/', (c) => c.text('QUERY /'))

// Wildcard
app.get('/wild/*/card', (c) => {
  return c.text('GET /wild/*/card')
})

// Any HTTP methods
app.all('/hello', (c) => c.text('Any Method /hello'))

// Custom HTTP method
app.on('PURGE', '/cache', (c) => c.text('PURGE Method /cache'))

// Multiple Method
app.on(['PUT', 'DELETE'], '/post', (c) =>
  c.text('PUT or DELETE /post')
)

// Multiple Paths
app.on('GET', ['/hello', '/ja/hello', '/en/hello'], (c) =>
  c.text('Hello')
)
```

--------------------------------

### startTime(c, name)

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/middleware/builtin/timing.md

Starts a timer for measuring the duration of a specific operation.

```APIDOC
### Description
Starts a performance timer under a given metric name for the current request context.

### Signature
`startTime(c, name)`

### Parameters
- **c** (Context) - Required - The Hono request context.
- **name** (string) - Required - Name identifier for the timer.

### Example
```ts
startTime(c, 'db')
const data = await db.findMany(...)
endTime(c, 'db')
```
```

### Create a basic GET endpoint returning JSON

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/concepts/stacks.md

Sets up a Hono application instance and defines a basic GET endpoint that responds with JSON.

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'

const app = new Hono()

app.get('/hello', (c) => {
  return c.json({
    message: `Hello!`,
  })
})
```

### Initialize CDK project with package manager

Initialize a TypeScript CDK application and install dependencies for Hono and @hono/lambda-edge using your preferred package manager.

```sh

--------------------------------

### Serve static files with @hono/bun serveStatic

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/getting-started/bun.md

Install the @hono/bun package and configure serveStatic middleware routes matching your file tree structure.

```sh
bun add @hono/bun
```

```ts
import { serveStatic } from '@hono/bun'

const app = new Hono()

app.use('/static/*', serveStatic({ root: './' }))
app.use('/favicon.ico', serveStatic({ path: './favicon.ico' }))
app.get('/', (c) => c.text('You can access: /static/hello.txt'))
app.get('*', serveStatic({ path: './static/fallback.txt' }))
```

```txt
./
├── favicon.ico
├── src
└── static
    ├── demo
    │   └── index.html
    ├── fallback.txt
    ├── hello.txt
    └── images
        └── dinotocat.png
```

### Testing Hono application with Deno.test and @std/assert

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/getting-started/deno.md

Install @std/assert, define a test file in hello.ts using app.request(), and run tests using the Deno CLI.

```sh
deno add jsr:@std/assert
```

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'
import { assertEquals } from '@std/assert'

Deno.test('Hello World', async () => {
  const app = new Hono()
  app.get('/', (c) => c.text('Please test me'))

  const res = await app.request('http://localhost/')
  assertEquals(res.status, 200)
})
```

```sh
deno test hello.ts
```

### Redirect GET requests with trimTrailingSlash

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/middleware/builtin/trailing-slash.md

Trims trailing slashes from URLs on GET requests when the response status is 404.

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'
import { trimTrailingSlash } from 'hono/trailing-slash'

const app = new Hono({ strict: true })

app.use(trimTrailingSlash())
app.get('/about/me', (c) => c.text('Without Trailing Slash'))
```

### Example JSON output from hono init

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/agents/cli.md

Shows the JSON result of `hono init`, including the selected template, the file it was detected from, files written, and files skipped because they already exist. Existing files are never overwritten and are listed in `skipped`; `package.json` is merged with existing values winning except `type`, which the template sets to `module`.

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "data": {
    "template": "cloudflare-workers",
    "detectedFrom": "wrangler.jsonc",
    "written": ["src/index.ts"],
    "skipped": ["wrangler.jsonc"]
  }
}
```

### Configuring default router with SmartRouter in Hono

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/concepts/routers.md

Illustrates how Hono initializes SmartRouter with RegExpRouter and TrieRouter by default. SmartRouter automatically detects the fastest compatible router based on registered routes upon application start.

```typescript
// Inside the core of Hono.
readonly defaultRouter: Router = new SmartRouter({
  routers: [new RegExpRouter(), new TrieRouter()],
})
```

### Create a Hello World handler for Netlify Edge Functions

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/getting-started/netlify.md

```ts
import { Hono } from 'jsr:@hono/hono'
import { handle } from 'jsr:@hono/netlify'

const app = new Hono()

app.get('/', (c) => {
  return c.text('Hello Hono!')
})

export default handle(app)
```

### Test GET request with app.request

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/guides/testing.md

```ts
describe('Example', () => {

    const res = await app.request('/posts')
    expect(res.status).toBe(200)
    expect(await res.text()).toBe('Many posts')
  })
})
```

--------------------------------

### Filter only GET requests with beforeRequestHook

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/helpers/ssg.md

Plugin that allows only GET requests to be processed. Non-GET requests are skipped by returning false.

```ts
const getOnlyPlugin: SSGPlugin = {
  beforeRequestHook: (req) => {
    if (req.method === 'GET') {
      return req
    }
    return false
  },
}
```

--------------------------------

### Set up WebSocket with upgradeWebSocket

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/getting-started/nodejs.md

Enable WebSocket support in @hono/node-server using ws and WebSocketServer with noServer set to true.

```ts
import { serve, upgradeWebSocket } from '@hono/node-server'
import { Hono } from 'hono'
import { WebSocketServer } from 'ws'

const app = new Hono()

app.get(
  '/ws',
  upgradeWebSocket(() => ({
    onMessage(event, ws) {
      ws.send(event.data)
    },
  }))
)

const wss = new WebSocketServer({ noServer: true })

serve({
  fetch: app.fetch,
  websocket: { server: wss },
})
```

### Create index.html entrypoint

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/getting-started/service-worker.md

Provide a link to trigger the Service Worker route and load the registration module main.ts.

```html
<!doctype html>
<html>
  <body>
    <a href="/sw">Hello World by Service Worker</a>
    <script type="module" src="/main.ts"></script>
  </body>
</html>
```

### Test GET request with app.request

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/api/hono.md

Use app.request to send a GET request by pathname and assert the response status. The app returns a Response object.

```typescript
import { Hono } from 'hono'
const app = new Hono()
declare const test: (name: string, fn: () => void) => void
declare const expect: (value: any) => any
// ---cut---
test('GET /hello is ok', async () => {
  const res = await app.request('/hello')
  expect(res.status).toBe(200)
})
```

--------------------------------

### endTime(c, name)

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/middleware/builtin/timing.md

Stops a previously started timer and records the duration in the metrics.

```APIDOC
### Description
Stops an active timer identified by name and calculates the elapsed duration for the Server-Timing header.

### Signature
`endTime(c, name)`

### Parameters
- **c** (Context) - Required - The Hono request context.
- **name** (string) - Required - Name identifier for the timer that was started.

### Example
```ts
startTime(c, 'db')
const data = await db.findMany(...)
endTime(c, 'db')
```
```

### Create and configure scf_bootstrap script

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/getting-started/cloudbase.md

Create scf_bootstrap in the project root with LF line endings and make it executable. Ensure the node path matches the target runtime (/var/lang/node20/bin/node for Node.js 20.19).

```sh
#!/bin/bash
/var/lang/node20/bin/node dist/index.js
```

```sh
chmod +x scf_bootstrap
```

--------------------------------

### Enable compressed static assets with precompressed

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/getting-started/deno.md

Serve precompressed .br or .gz files automatically based on the client's Accept-Encoding header, prioritizing Brotli, Zstd, then Gzip before falling back to the raw file.

```ts
app.get(
  '/static/*',
  serveStatic({
    precompressed: true,
  })
)
```

--------------------------------

### Get all matched routes with matchedRoutes()

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/helpers/route.md

Returns an array of all routes and middleware matching the current request.

```ts
app.all('/api/*', (c, next) => {
  console.log('API middleware')
  return next()
})

app.get('/api/users/:id', (c) => {
  const routes = matchedRoutes(c)
  // Returns: [
  //   { method: 'ALL', path: '/api/*', handler: [Function] },
  //   { method: 'GET', path: '/api/users/:id', handler: [Function] }
  // ]
  return c.json({ routes: routes.length })
})
```

--------------------------------

### Get current route pattern with routePath()

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/helpers/route.md

Returns the registered route path pattern for the current handler.

```ts
app.get('/posts/:id', (c) => {
  console.log(routePath(c)) // '/posts/:id'
  return c.text('Post details')
})
```

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/helpers/dev.md

Returns the name of the router currently being used by the Hono application instance.

```ts
const app = new Hono()

// ...

console.log(getRouterName(app))
```

### Use Server-Timing middleware with metrics and timers

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/middleware/builtin/timing.md

Demonstrates applying the `timing` middleware to a Hono app, recording string and numeric metrics with `setMetric`, and measuring execution durations with `startTime`/`endTime` or `wrapTime`.

```js
// Specify the variable types to infer the `c.get('metric')`:
type Variables = TimingVariables

const app = new Hono<{ Variables: Variables }>()

// add the middleware to your router
app.use(timing());

app.get('/', async (c) => {

  // add custom metrics
  setMetric(c, 'region', 'europe-west3')

  // add custom metrics with timing, must be in milliseconds
  setMetric(c, 'custom', 23.8, 'My custom Metric')

  // start a new timer
  startTime(c, 'db');
  const data = await db.findMany(...);

  // end the timer
  endTime(c, 'db');

  // ...or you can also just wrap a Promise using this function:
  const data = await wrapTime(c, 'db', db.findMany(...));

  return c.json({ response: data });
});
```

--------------------------------

### showRoutes(app, options?)

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/helpers/dev.md

Prints all registered application routes to the console. Supports optional configuration for verbose output and color formatting.

```APIDOC
## showRoutes(app, options?)

### Description
Displays the registered routes in the console when the application starts or runs.

### Syntax
`showRoutes(app, options?)`

### Parameters
- **app** (`Hono`) - Required - The Hono application instance containing registered routes.
- **options** (`object`) - Optional - Configuration options for route display:
  - **verbose** (`boolean`) - Optional - When set to `true`, displays verbose information.
  - **colorize** (`boolean`) - Optional - When set to `false`, the output will not be colored.

### Example
```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'
import { showRoutes } from 'hono/dev'

const app = new Hono().basePath('/v1')

app.get('/posts', (c) => {})
app.get('/posts/:id', (c) => {})
app.post('/posts', (c) => {})

showRoutes(app, {
  verbose: true,
})
```
```

--------------------------------

### Get basic route information

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/helpers/route.md

Access the current route pattern and all matched routes within a request handler.

```ts
const app = new Hono()

app.get('/posts/:id', (c) => {
  const currentPath = routePath(c) // '/posts/:id'
  const routes = matchedRoutes(c) // Array of matched routes

  return c.json({
    path: currentPath,
    totalRoutes: routes.length,
  })
})
```

### Get request header values with c.req.header()

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/api/request.md

Retrieve specific HTTP request headers such as User-Agent using c.req.header().

```typescript
import { Hono } from 'hono'
const app = new Hono()
// ---cut---
app.get('/', (c) => {
  const userAgent = c.req.header('User-Agent')
  //      ^?
  return c.text(`Your user agent is ${userAgent}`)
})
```

--------------------------------

### Create auth API handler in routes/auth.ts

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/examples/better-auth.md

Serves all POST and GET requests under /auth/* by delegating to auth.handler with the raw request.

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'
import { auth } from '../lib/auth'
import type { AuthType } from '../lib/auth'

const router = new Hono<{ Bindings: AuthType }>({
  strict: false,
})

router.on(['POST', 'GET'], '/auth/*', (c) => {
  return auth.handler(c.req.raw)
})

export default router
```

### Deploying a minified application using PatternRouter

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/concepts/routers.md

Shows output from deploying a minified Hono application with PatternRouter via Wrangler. PatternRouter produces compact build outputs under 15KB for environments with strict resource constraints.

```console
$ npx wrangler deploy --minify ./src/index.ts
 ⛅️ wrangler 3.20.0
-------------------
Total Upload: 14.68 KiB / gzip: 5.38 KiB
```

### Get resolved base path with basePath()

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/helpers/route.md

Returns the base path including resolved parameter values from the actual request.

```ts
const subApp = new Hono()
subApp.get('/posts/:id', (c) => {
  return c.text(basePath(c)) // '/api' (for request to '/api/posts/123')
})

app.route('/:sub', subApp)
```

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'
import {
  contextStorage,
  getContext,
  tryGetContext,
} from 'hono/context-storage'
```

### Get base route pattern with baseRoutePath()

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/helpers/route.md

Returns the base path pattern of the current route as defined during sub-app routing.

```ts
const subApp = new Hono()
subApp.get('/posts/:id', (c) => {
  return c.text(baseRoutePath(c)) // '/:sub'
})

app.route('/:sub', subApp)
```

--------------------------------

### Get route path at index with routePath()

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/helpers/route.md

Pass an index parameter to routePath() to retrieve the route path at a specific position.

```ts
app.all('/api/*', (c, next) => {
  return next()
})

app.get('/api/users/:id', (c) => {
  console.log(routePath(c, 0)) // '/api/*' (first matched route)
  console.log(routePath(c, -1)) // '/api/users/:id' (last matched route)
  return c.text('User details')
})
```

### Get multiple query parameters with c.req.queries()

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/api/request.md

Retrieve multiple values for duplicate query parameter keys as an array of strings.

```typescript
import { Hono } from 'hono'
const app = new Hono()
// ---cut---
app.get('/search', async (c) => {
  // tags will be string[]
  const tags = c.req.queries('tags')
  //     ^?
  // ...
})
```
